5289.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂enǵʰ- (“to constrict”). Cognates include Old English enge (whence the first element in English hangnail), Latin angō, Sanskrit अंहु (áṃhu), and Old Armenian անձուկ (anjuk, “narrow; tight”).

5272.t: Generally considered to be a derivation in "-λ-" of ὀστέον (ostéon, “bone”), but this cannot be correct. According to Beekes, it is probably a Pre-Greek word.

5282.t: From ἀ- (a-) + ὁρατός (horātós, “seen”), verbal adjective of ὁράω (horáō).

5201.t: It matches Thracian Ἀλαζών (Alazṓn) exactly, perhaps an appellative, or it may be a cultural loanword from Akkadian 𒀀𒇻𒍣𒉡 aluzinnu, 'boastful, clownish fraud, most times pretending or claiming to possess medical skills or knowledge.' From Sumerian 𒀩𒍪…

5205.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + μέθυστος (méthŭstos, “drunken”), from μεθύω (methŭ́ō, “to be drunk on wine”), from μέθυ (méthŭ, “wine”). Compare to εὐμέθυστος (euméthŭstos, “easily made drunk”).

5276.t: From ἀτενής (atenḗs, “intent”) + -ίζω (-ízō, denominative verb suffix), from τείνω (teínō, “to strain, to exert”).

5277.t: According to De Vaan, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ét(i). Compare Tocharian B ate (“away”).

5233.t: From ἀντίος (antíos): the adverb/preposition is from the adverbial accusative, and the noun is from the neuter singular.

5221.t: From ἀνδρεῖος (andreîos, “manly”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun–forming suffix). Compare ἠνορέη (ēnoréē).

5287.t: From ἀγάλλομαι (agállomai, “to be proud, exult in”) + -μα (-ma).

5281.t: Loaned from a non-Indo-European source, possibly Semitic (compare Aramaic עקיק). The river Ἀχάτης in Sicily is probably named after the mineral.

5215.t: From ἀνα- (“backwords”) + πούς (gentive: ποδός) (“foot”) + -ίζω (“suffix for verbs”).

5297.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ároura, from the Proto-Indo-European heteroclitic noun *h₂érh₃-wr̥ ~ *h₂r̥h₃-wén-s, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂erh₃-.

5266.t: A loanword from Biblical Hebrew עירבון / עֵרָבוֹן (ʿērāḇōn, “guarantee, deposit”), or from a common third source, probably Semitic.

5264.t: From ἀποδείκνυμι (apodeíknūmi, “to show, display”) + -σις (-sis, verbal noun suffix).

5216.t: From ἀνα- (ana-, intensifying affix) + σπάω (spáō, “to draw”)
